models.name: discussion_board_users
models.description:
Regular user accounts with email/password authentication credentials and profile information for discussion board participation.

Stores core identity information for registered users including authentication credentials, account status, and basic profile data. Each user account enables full platform participation including article creation, commenting, and profile management.

The table maintains authentication requirements including unique email validation, password hashing, email verification status, and account activation controls. User accounts can be in various states including pending verification, active, suspended, or banned, with appropriate access restrictions.

Account lifecycle management includes creation timestamps, last login tracking, and soft deletion capability through deleted_at field. All user personal data follows platform privacy policies and authentication security standards.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: User's unique email address used for authentication and communication. Must be unique across all user accounts.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Hashed password string for secure user authentication. Never stored in plain text format.

plainFields.name: display_name
plainFields.description: User's public display name shown on articles, comments, and profile. Can be updated by the user.

plainFields.name: account_status
plainFields.description: Current status of the user account. Valid values: pending_verification, active, suspended, banned.

plainFields.name: email_verified
plainFields.description: Whether the user's email address has been successfully verified through the verification process.

plainFields.name: last_login_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the user's most recent successful login for activity tracking.

plainFields.name: failed_login_attempts
plainFields.description: Count of consecutive failed login attempts for security monitoring and account lockout prevention.

plainFields.name: account_locked_until
plainFields.description: Timestamp until which the account is locked due to excessive failed login attempts.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the user account was initially created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the user account was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the user account was soft deleted, allowing for account recovery.

models.name: discussion_board_user_sessions
models.description:
User authentication session tokens implementing JWT-based authentication with 15-minute access tokens and 30-day refresh tokens as specified in requirements.

Stores connection context including IP address, URL, and referrer for session tracking and security audits. Each session belongs to exactly one user and maintains authentication state until expiration.

Sessions are automatically invalidated upon password changes or explicit logout, and expired sessions are periodically cleaned up by the system to maintain security compliance.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_user_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged user's {@link discussion_board_users.id}.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address of the connection that created this session for security tracking.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: Connection URL where the session was initiated for contextual logging.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: Referrer URL that brought the user to the session creation endpoint.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Session creation timestamp when the user successfully authenticated.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Session expiration timestamp when the session becomes invalid - sessions must expire for security.

models.name: discussion_board_user_password_resets
models.description:
Password reset tokens with expiration for secure user password recovery workflow.

Stores temporary tokens that allow users to reset their passwords securely. Each token is valid for a limited time period (typically 1 hour) and can only be used once. The system generates unique tokens when users request password resets and invalidates them after successful usage or expiration.

Tokens reference the target user through foreign key relationship and include expiration timestamps for automatic cleanup. This table supports the password recovery functionality required by the authentication system while maintaining security through token expiration and single-use constraints.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_user_id
foreignFields.description: The user requesting password reset. {@link discussion_board_users.id}

plainFields.name: token
plainFields.description: Unique password reset token generated for secure password recovery process. Tokens are cryptographically secure and can only be used once.

plainFields.name: expires_at
plainFields.description: Token expiration timestamp after which the password reset token becomes invalid for security.

plainFields.name: used_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the password reset token was successfully used to reset the password, marking it as consumed.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the password reset token was initially created for the user's request.

models.name: discussion_board_user_email_verifications
models.description:
Email verification tokens for user registration confirmation with 24-hour expiration.

Stores verification tokens sent to users during the registration process to validate email addresses. Each token is associated with a specific user account and has a limited validity period as specified in the authentication requirements.

The system generates unique tokens for each verification request and tracks whether the token has been used to confirm the email address. Tokens expire after 24 hours to maintain security and prevent unauthorized account activation.

This table supports the email verification workflow required for user registration, ensuring that only valid email addresses can be used to create accounts on the discussion board platform.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_user_id
foreignFields.description: Associated user account requiring email verification. {@link discussion_board_users.id}

plainFields.name: token
plainFields.description: Unique verification token sent to the user's email address for account confirmation. Must be cryptographically secure and unique per verification request.

plainFields.name: verified
plainFields.description: Indicates whether the email verification has been completed successfully. Set to true when the user clicks the verification link.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the verification token was created and sent to the user.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the verification token expires, typically 24 hours after creation as specified in requirements.

plainFields.name: verified_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the email verification was successfully completed. Null until verification occurs.

models.name: discussion_board_administrators
models.description:
Administrator accounts with elevated privileges for content moderation and section management.

Stores authentication credentials and administrative profile information for users granted elevated permissions to manage the discussion platform. Administrators inherit all regular user capabilities while gaining additional administrative functions including section management, content moderation, and user supervision.

Each administrator account references a corresponding user account using inheritance pattern, maintaining separate authentication credentials while preserving shared user functionality. This enables administrator accounts to participate in discussion activities while also performing administrative duties.

Administrators require email verification for account activation and maintain separate credential management from regular users for security purposes. The account lifecycle includes registration, verification, activation, and potential deactivation or deletion workflows.

Soft deletion support allows temporary account suspension while preserving administrative action audit trails and maintaining referential integrity across the system.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_user_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the base user account from which this administrator inherits. {@link discussion_board_users.id}

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Unique email address used for administrator authentication and communication. Must follow valid email format and remain unique across all administrator accounts.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Securely hashed password for administrator authentication using industry-standard cryptographic hashing algorithms. Never stored in plain text.

plainFields.name: email_verified
plainFields.description: Indicates whether the administrator's email address has been successfully verified. Required for full account activation and administrative access.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the administrator account was originally created in the system.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the administrator account was last modified, including profile updates or credential changes.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the administrator account was soft deleted, allowing for account recovery while maintaining audit trails.

models.name: discussion_board_administrator_sessions
models.description:
JWT session tokens for administrator authentication with access and refresh token support.

Stores administrator login sessions with connection context including IP address, URL, and referrer information. Each session has expiration tracking for security compliance. Sessions are managed through authentication workflows and support the required session management functionality.

Follows the standardized session table pattern for consistency across actor types in the authorization domain.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_administrator_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the administrator account managing this session. {@link discussion_board_administrators.id}

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address of the connection where the session was created. Used for security monitoring and geographic tracking.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: Full URL of the page where the session was initiated. Provides context for session creation for auditing purposes.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: Referrer URL that directed the user to the session creation page. Used for traffic source analysis and audit trails.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session was created. Used for session lifecycle management and expiration calculations.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session expires. Sessions must expire for security compliance as specified in requirements.

models.name: discussion_board_administrator_password_resets
models.description:
Password reset tokens for administrator accounts with expiration for secure password recovery workflow.

Stores temporary tokens that allow administrators to reset their passwords when forgotten. Contains the reset token, expiration timestamp, and references the specific administrator account requesting reset.

Tokens are single-use and expire after a configurable period for security. Requires valid administrator authentication and session validation to initiate password reset process. Follows same security patterns as user password reset functionality.

The system automatically invalidates tokens after use or expiration to prevent unauthorized access. Administrators can initiate reset requests through authenticated interfaces only.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_administrator_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the authenticated administrator's {@link discussion_board_administrators.id} who requested password reset.

plainFields.name: token
plainFields.description: Secure reset token used for password reset validation. Generated as cryptographically secure random string.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Expiration timestamp for the reset token. After this time, the token becomes invalid for security.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the password reset request was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the password reset record was last updated.

models.name: discussion_board_administrator_email_verifications
models.description:
Email verification tokens for validating administrator email addresses during registration.

Stores unique tokens sent to administrator email addresses for confirmation of account ownership. Each token expires 24 hours after creation as required by the authentication specifications. Tokens are consumed upon successful verification and remain for audit purposes.

The verification process ensures only email-verified administrators can access the platform, maintaining security and preventing unauthorized account creation. Failed verification attempts are logged for security monitoring.

Administrator registration requires email confirmation before full account activation, following the specified workflow where registration sends verification email that must be completed within the expiration period.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_administrator_id
foreignFields.description: Verification token belongs to the target administrator's {@link discussion_board_administrators.id}.

plainFields.name: token
plainFields.description: Unique verification token sent via email to confirm administrator email address ownership. Must be cryptographically secure and globally unique.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Token expiration timestamp. Tokens expire 24 hours after creation as specified in authentication requirements, after which they cannot be used.

plainFields.name: verified_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when email verification was successfully completed. Null indicates pending verification status.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Creation timestamp for the verification token, used for tracking token lifecycle and audit purposes.

models.name: discussion_board_super_administrators
models.description:
Highest-level administrator accounts with ultimate system authority and administrative oversight.

Represents super administrators who have the highest privileges in the discussion board system, including the ability to manage other administrators, approve promotion requests, and perform all system functions. These accounts use the same authentication patterns as regular administrators with email/password login and session management.

Super administrators cannot be demoted except by other super administrators, ensuring system oversight continuity. These accounts have comprehensive access to all administrative functions while maintaining separate authentication from regular administrator accounts for security and audit purposes.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Email address used for authentication. Must be unique across all super administrator accounts for login purposes.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Hashed password using secure hashing algorithm for authentication security. Required for login functionality.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Account status indicating current state: active, suspended, or pending. Controls authentication and access privileges.

plainFields.name: failed_login_attempts
plainFields.description: Count of consecutive failed login attempts for security monitoring and account lockout protection.

plainFields.name: last_login_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of last successful login for security monitoring and user activity tracking.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the super administrator account was created for audit trail and account lifecycle tracking.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the super administrator account was last updated for change tracking and audit purposes.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the super administrator account was soft deleted for recovery capability and audit preservation.

models.name: discussion_board_super_administrator_sessions
models.description:
JWT session tokens for super administrator authentication with access and refresh token support.

Stores connection context and authentication tokens for super administrator login sessions as specified in requirements. Each session tracks the connection metadata including IP address, connection URL, referrer, and session timestamps for security auditing.

The session implements the required security features including automatic expiration for access tokens and session invalidation mechanisms. Support for JWT token refresh maintains session continuity while enforcing security policies.

Super administrator sessions follow the same authentication patterns as other actor types but with elevated administrative privileges and extended oversight capabilities for system management functions.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_super_administrator_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the super administrator's primary key. {@link discussion_board_super_administrators.id}

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address of the connection that created the session. Used for security auditing and connection tracking.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: URL of the connection that initiated the session. Records the initial access point for audit purposes.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: Referrer URL that directed the super administrator to the session start point. Used for traffic analysis and security monitoring.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session was created. Used for session lifecycle tracking and audit trail maintenance.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session expires for security compliance. All sessions must have expiration for security reasons.

models.name: discussion_board_super_administrator_password_resets
models.description:
Password reset tokens for super administrators with expiration tracking for secure password recovery.

Provides temporary token-based authentication for super administrators requesting password resets. Each token has a specific expiration period to maintain security while allowing legitimate password recovery operations. Links directly to the corresponding super administrator account for identity verification.

Following authentication security best practices, these tokens enable super administrators to regain access to their accounts securely without compromising system integrity. The tokens expire automatically after their designated lifespan to prevent unauthorized use.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_super_administrator_id
foreignFields.description: Associated super administrator initiating the password reset request. {@link discussion_board_super_administrators.id}

plainFields.name: token
plainFields.description: Secure reset token generated for password recovery authentication. Must be unique and cryptographically secure.

plainFields.name: expires_at
plainFields.description: Token expiration timestamp for security. Password reset tokens must expire to prevent unauthorized access.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the password reset token was created for audit trail purposes.

plainFields.name: used_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the token was successfully used to reset the password, null until utilized.

models.name: discussion_board_super_administrator_email_verifications
models.description:
Email verification tokens for super administrator registration confirmation.

Handles the email verification workflow required for super administrator account activation as specified in authentication requirements. Each token has a 24-hour expiration period from creation time to ensure timely verification.

Tokens are generated during super administrator registration and must be verified before full account activation. Verification attempts are tracked to detect suspicious activity or repeated verification failures.

This table supports the security requirement that all super administrator accounts must complete email verification before gaining full system access, ensuring proper authorization and accountability for the highest privilege level.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_super_administrator_id
foreignFields.description: Target super administrator awaiting email verification. {@link discussion_board_super_administrators.id}

plainFields.name: token
plainFields.description: Unique verification token sent to super administrator's email address for account verification.

plainFields.name: expires_at
plainFields.description: Expiration timestamp for the verification token with 24-hour validity period from creation time.

plainFields.name: verified_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when email verification was successfully completed by the super administrator.

plainFields.name: verification_attempts
plainFields.description: Number of verification attempts made with this token to detect suspicious activity patterns.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the verification token was created during super administrator registration.

models.name: discussion_board_sections
models.description:
Discussion board sections provide the primary organizational structure for categorizing articles by topic areas such as Politics, Economy, and Current Affairs.

Each section serves as a container for articles on specific topics, enabling users to browse content within specialized domains. Sections are created and managed exclusively by administrators to maintain organizational consistency and content quality standards.

The unique naming requirement ensures sections maintain clear identity within the platform, while descriptions provide users with clear context about each section's focus and purpose. Section lifecycle management includes activation/deactivation capabilities to support platform evolution.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Unique section name used for identification and display purposes. Must be unique across all sections and follow naming conventions (3-50 characters).

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Detailed description explaining the section's purpose, focus area, and content scope for user guidance (10-200 characters).

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Section status indicating whether active for content creation or inactive for maintenance or restructuring purposes.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the section was first created by an administrator.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the section was last modified, including configuration changes or status updates.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the section was soft-deleted for archive purposes, nullable for active sections.

models.name: discussion_board_channels
models.description:
Platform channels providing organizational structure for the discussion board with configuration settings.

Channels serve as high-level organizational units that group related sections and apply uniform configuration settings across the discussion board platform. Each channel represents a distinct organizational boundary with specific settings, access controls, and content organization rules.

Channels reference existing sections through many-to-one relationships, allowing sections to be grouped logically under channel hierarchies. Configuration inheritance is managed directly through channel-level settings, which may override or supplement system-wide configurations.

The channel structure enables multi-tenant or departmental organization of discussion content while maintaining centralized administration and moderation capabilities. Channel-specific settings can include display preferences, access restrictions, moderation workflows, and content organization rules.

Each channel must have at least one section assigned to provide content structure, and configuration settings define the operational parameters for all content within the channel boundary.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_section_id
foreignFields.description: Primary section hosted within this channel for content organization. {@link discussion_board_sections.id}

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_configuration_id
foreignFields.description: Channel-specific configuration settings. {@link discussion_board_configurations.id}

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Unique channel name for identification and display purposes (3-50 characters).

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Channel description explaining the purpose and scope of the organizational unit (10-200 characters).

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the channel was created for audit trail purposes.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the channel was last updated for change tracking.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the channel was soft-deleted, supporting content preservation.

models.name: discussion_board_configurations
models.description:
System-wide configuration definitions and metadata for platform customization.

Stores the definition of all available configuration settings including their data types, validation rules, and descriptions. Each configuration represents a system-wide setting that can be customized to control platform behavior, feature availability, or user experience.

Configurations support multiple data types including boolean flags, string values, numeric settings, and JSON objects. Each configuration includes validation rules to ensure data integrity and consistency across the platform.

Administrators can manage these configurations to enable/disable features, set global parameters, and customize the platform's behavior without requiring code changes.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Unique identifier for the configuration setting. Used as the key for programmatic access and API references.

plainFields.name: type
plainFields.description: Type of configuration value. Valid values: boolean, string, integer, double, json - determines how the value is validated and processed.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Human-readable description explaining the purpose and usage of this configuration setting.

plainFields.name: default_value
plainFields.description: Default value for this configuration when no custom value is set. Must be valid for the specified type.

plainFields.name: validation_rules
plainFields.description: JSON object containing validation rules specific to the configuration type. Examples: min/max for numbers, patterns for strings, schema for JSON.

plainFields.name: scope
plainFields.description: Scope of this configuration. Valid values: global, user, administrator, super_administrator, section. Determines where this configuration applies.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this configuration definition was first created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this configuration definition was last modified.

models.name: discussion_board_configuration_values
models.description:
Actual configuration values stored for different scopes and contexts.

Stores the current active values for configuration settings across different scopes. Each value is associated with a specific configuration definition and may apply globally or to specific entities like users, administrators, or sections.

Allows for hierarchical configuration where specific scopes can override global defaults. Values are validated against their configuration's type and validation rules to ensure data integrity.

This table enables flexible platform customization where different sections or user types can have unique configurations while maintaining a consistent configuration management interface.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_configuration_id
foreignFields.description: References the configuration definition this value applies to. {@link discussion_board_configurations.id}

plainFields.name: scope
plainFields.description: Scope context for this configuration value. If global, applies to entire platform. Other values reference specific entity types.

plainFields.name: target_id
plainFields.description: Optional target entity ID when scope is specific (e.g., user_id, section_id). Null for global scope.

plainFields.name: value
plainFields.description: Current configuration value. Must be valid according to the associated configuration's type and validation rules.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this configuration value was first set.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this configuration value was last modified.

models.name: discussion_board_configuration_snapshots
models.description:
Historical snapshots of configuration changes for audit trail and rollback capabilities.

Tracks all changes made to configuration values over time, preserving the complete history of platform settings. Each snapshot captures the configuration value at a specific point in time along with metadata about the change.

Supports audit requirements by recording who made changes, when they were made, and what the previous values were. Enables administrators to review configuration history and potentially roll back to previous settings if needed.

Maintains data integrity by ensuring configuration changes are properly documented and traceable throughout the platform's lifecycle.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_configuration_value_id
foreignFields.description: References the configuration value that was modified. {@link discussion_board_configuration_values.id}

plainFields.name: previous_value
plainFields.description: Previous configuration value before this change was made. Allows for comparison and rollback capabilities.

plainFields.name: new_value
plainFields.description: New configuration value after this change was applied.

plainFields.name: changed_by_user_id
plainFields.description: ID of the user or administrator who made this configuration change. References appropriate user/administrator table.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Optional reason provided for this configuration change. Used for audit trail and documentation purposes.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this configuration snapshot was created (when the change occurred).

models.name: discussion_board_user_profiles
models.description:
User profile information storing display name, biography text, and visibility settings.

Contains publicly visible profile data that users can customize, including display name for identification and biography text for personal information sharing. Profile settings control visibility and accessibility preferences across the platform.

The profile serves as the public-facing identity separate from authentication credentials, allowing users to maintain consistent personal presentation while keeping security information private. Profiles are independently managed by users through dedicated profile editing interfaces while maintaining the 1:1 relationship with user identities.

Linked to the main user identity record for authentication and access control. Profile updates maintain audit trail through timestamp tracking and historical records. Profile visibility settings control public access while maintaining administrative visibility for moderation purposes.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_user_id
foreignFields.description: Associated user identity's Primary Key. Links to the authentication and identity management system for user account reference. {@link discussion_board_users.id}

plainFields.name: display_name
plainFields.description: User's public display name shown throughout the platform. Maximum 50 characters alphanumeric with spaces and basic punctuation. Must be unique across the system for user identification.

plainFields.name: bio
plainFields.description: User biography text providing personal information and introduction. Maximum 500 characters plain text supporting basic formatting. Optional field for user self-expression.

plainFields.name: profile_visible
plainFields.description: Controls whether profile information is publicly accessible to other users. When false, profile details are hidden from public view while maintaining administrative access for moderation and auditing.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Profile creation timestamp recording when the user profile was initially created during account registration or profile setup.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Profile last modification timestamp tracking when profile information was last updated by the user or system.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp indicating when the profile was marked for removal. Null indicates active profile, timestamp indicates deletion time.

models.name: discussion_board_profile_statistics
models.description:
Calculated statistics and activity metrics for user profiles, providing quantitative insights into user engagement and participation.

Tracks quantitative measurements of user activity including article creation counts, comment frequency, section participation, and temporal patterns of engagement. These statistics are automatically calculated and updated based on user actions to provide comprehensive profile analytics.

The statistics enable features like profile completeness indicators, user activity insights, and engagement tracking across different sections of the discussion board. Administrators can use these metrics to identify highly active users and understand platform usage patterns.

Each statistics record maintains a 1:1 relationship with its parent user profile, ensuring statistical data remains synchronized with profile changes and user activity updates.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_user_profile_id
foreignFields.description: Associated user profile's unique identifier. {@link discussion_board_user_profiles.id}

plainFields.name: total_articles
plainFields.description: Total count of articles created by the user across all sections of the platform.

plainFields.name: politics_articles
plainFields.description: Count of articles created by the user specifically in the Politics section. Helps identify user's focus area.

plainFields.name: economy_articles
plainFields.description: Count of articles created by the user specifically in the Economy section. Tracks user's subject matter expertise.

plainFields.name: current_affairs_articles
plainFields.description: Count of articles created by the user specifically in the Current Affairs section. Measures topical engagement.

plainFields.name: total_comments
plainFields.description: Total count of comments written by the user across all articles on the platform. Reflects user's engagement level.

plainFields.name: comment_characters
plainFields.description: Total character count across all user comments. Provides insight into comment quality and depth of engagement.

plainFields.name: average_comment_length
plainFields.description: Average character length of user comments. Calculated as comment_characters ÷ total_comments.

plainFields.name: last_article_created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the most recent article created by the user. Indicates recent activity level and engagement.

plainFields.name: last_comment_created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the most recent comment posted by the user. Helps track current engagement and participation habits.

plainFields.name: days_active
plainFields.description: Number of unique days the user has been active on the platform (created content or engaged in discussions).

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this statistics record was first created. Usually coincides with profile creation.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this statistics record was last updated with new activity data.

models.name: discussion_board_profile_view_logs
models.description:
Audit trail tracking when users view other users' profiles for analytics and moderation.

Records captures viewing activity between users to monitor engagement patterns and support moderation workflows. Each entry logs a specific viewing event with timestamps and user references.

The data collected enables analysis of user interaction patterns, profile popularity metrics, and identification of potential stalking or harassment behaviors that might require administrative intervention.

The audit trail maintains referential integrity through foreign key relationships to both the viewing user and the profile being viewed, ensuring accurate tracking of profile viewing activity across the platform.

foreignFields.name: viewer_id
foreignFields.description: User who viewed the profile. {@link discussion_board_users.id}

foreignFields.name: profile_id
foreignFields.description: Profile that was viewed. {@link discussion_board_user_profiles.id}

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the profile view occurred, used for chronological tracking and analytics.

models.name: discussion_board_profile_update_histories
models.description:
Historical audit trail tracking all modifications made to user profiles for transparency and accountability.

Stores comprehensive change records including display name updates, biography modifications, and any other profile field changes. Each record captures the exact timestamp of modification, the specific field that was changed, the previous value, and the new value.

Maintains complete audit history for compliance and user transparency requirements. Used for tracking profile evolution over time and providing rollback capability if needed. References the parent {@link discussion_board_user_profiles.id} to associate changes with specific user profiles.

This table follows append-only pattern and should never be modified or deleted once created to maintain audit integrity.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_user_profile_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the user profile that was modified. {@link discussion_board_user_profiles.id}

plainFields.name: field_name
plainFields.description: Name of the profile field that was modified (e.g., "display_name", "bio", "avatar_url").

plainFields.name: old_value
plainFields.description: Previous value of the field before the modification. Stores empty string if field was previously null.

plainFields.name: new_value
plainFields.description: New value of the field after the modification. Stores empty string if field was set to null.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Exact timestamp when the profile modification occurred.

models.name: discussion_board_section_statistics
models.description:
Tracks quantitative metrics and activity statistics for discussion board sections.

Maintains real-time statistics including article counts, comment volumes, engagement metrics, and last activity timestamps for each section. This enables section performance analysis, trending content identification, and administrative reporting.

The statistics are automatically updated by system triggers when articles, comments, or user interactions occur within sections. Each section maintains exactly one statistics record that evolves over time as activity increases.

Supports requirements for section-level analytics and administrative oversight of section engagement patterns.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_section_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the section these statistics measure. {@link discussion_board_sections.id}

plainFields.name: article_count
plainFields.description: Total number of articles published in this section. Increments automatically when new articles are created.

plainFields.name: comment_count
plainFields.description: Total number of comments across all articles in this section. Tracks overall discussion volume.

plainFields.name: total_views
plainFields.description: Cumulative count of all article and section page views within this section.

plainFields.name: unique_contributors
plainFields.description: Total distinct users who have contributed articles or comments to this section.

plainFields.name: last_article_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the most recent article published in this section. Null when no articles exist.

plainFields.name: last_comment_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the most recent comment posted in this section. Null when no comments exist.

plainFields.name: last_activity_at
plainFields.description: Latest timestamp of any activity (article, comment, view) in this section. Always reflects current engagement.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when statistics tracking began for this section.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the last statistics update for this section.

models.name: discussion_board_section_admins
models.description:
Manages administrator assignments to sections for content moderation and management responsibilities.

This junction table establishes many-to-many relationships between administrators and sections, tracking assignment lifecycle and status. Each assignment records when an administrator was assigned to a section, current assignment status, and provides audit trail capabilities for assignment changes.

Administrators can be assigned to multiple sections, and sections can have multiple administrators. The system maintains comprehensive tracking of assignment creation, modifications, and status changes to ensure proper access control and accountability for section-specific administrative functions.

Assignment status follows a managed lifecycle with clear transitions between active, inactive, and suspended states, with timestamps tracking each status change for audit purposes.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_administrator_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the assigned administrator responsible for section management. {@link discussion_board_administrators.id}

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_section_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the section being managed by the administrator. {@link discussion_board_sections.id}

plainFields.name: assigned_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the administrator was initially assigned to this section.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current assignment status. Valid values: active, inactive, suspended. Active assignments grant section management privileges.

plainFields.name: status_changed_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the assignment status was last changed. Used for audit trail and status change tracking.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this assignment record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this assignment record was last modified.

models.name: discussion_board_section_snapshots
models.description:
Historical snapshots of section configurations capturing point-in-time states for audit trail and version control functionality.

Each snapshot preserves the exact configuration state of a section at a specific moment in time, allowing administrators to track changes, revert configurations, and maintain comprehensive audit trails. Snapshots are automatically created when section configurations are modified, supporting regulatory compliance and administrative oversight.

The snapshots reference {@link discussion_board_sections.id} to maintain the historical relationship with the parent section entity while storing independent configuration states for version comparison and rollback capabilities.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_section_id
foreignFields.description: References the parent section configuration snapshot. {@link discussion_board_sections.id}

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Snapshot version of the section name captured at creation time for historical accuracy.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Snapshot version of the section description preserved for audit trail purposes.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this configuration snapshot was captured for audit trail purposes.

models.name: discussion_board_section_admin_permissions
models.description:
Stores permission definitions for administrator assignments to sections, enforcing First Normal Form compliance.

This child table decomposes the non-atomic permission data from the main assignment table, providing proper normalization and flexible permission management. Each permission record defines the specific access level granted to an administrator for a particular section assignment.

Permissions follow a hierarchical structure with clear role definitions that determine what administrative actions can be performed within the assigned section. This separation allows for flexible permission management without denormalizing the main assignment relationship.

The table supports multiple permission levels per assignment and maintains proper referential integrity with the parent assignment table.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_section_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the parent section administrator assignment. {@link discussion_board_section_admins.id}

plainFields.name: permission_level
plainFields.description: Specific permission level granted for this assignment. Valid values: moderator, manager, viewer. Controls administrative capabilities within the assigned section.

plainFields.name: granted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this specific permission was granted to the assignment.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this permission record was created.

models.name: discussion_board_articles
models.description:
Main article content storing titles, text content, and section assignments for the discussion board platform.

Hosts all published articles with their core content, metadata, and organizational relationships. Each article belongs to a specific section and has an author, enabling structured discussion organization. Articles support attachments and tagging through related tables for comprehensive content management.

The table implements standard audit trails with creation timestamps, modification tracking, and soft deletion capabilities. Title and content fields enforce character limits as specified in business requirements while supporting the platform's core discussion functionality.

Articles serve as the primary content entities that users create, read, and manage independently throughout their lifecycle.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_section_id
foreignFields.description: Assigned section for article categorization referencing {@link discussion_board_sections.id}.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_user_id
foreignFields.description: Article author referencing the user who created it {@link discussion_board_users.id}.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Article title with minimum 3 and maximum 200 character limit as required for content structure.

plainFields.name: content
plainFields.description: Article main text content with minimum 50 and maximum 10,000 character limit supporting detailed discussions.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the article was originally created by the author.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the article was last modified, updated on every content change.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the article was soft deleted, allowing content preservation and recovery.

models.name: discussion_board_article_files
models.description:
File attachments for articles stored with proper metadata and format validation.

Each file attachment links to a specific article and maintains comprehensive metadata including filename, size, MIME type, and storage information. Supports PDF, DOC, DOCX, TXT, and ZIP formats with validation to ensure only approved file types are accepted.

File attachments are managed through parent article operations and inherit the article's lifecycle. When articles are modified or deleted, associated file attachments follow the same operations through referential integrity constraints.

The table maintains strict format validation to ensure platform security and compatibility while providing flexible file attachment capabilities for article content enhancement.

Referencing parent article entity: {@link discussion_board_articles.id}

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_article_id
foreignFields.description: Parent article that this file attachment belongs to. {@link discussion_board_articles.id}

plainFields.name: filename
plainFields.description: Original filename of the uploaded file as provided by the user.

plainFields.name: file_size
plainFields.description: File size in bytes for storage management and validation.

plainFields.name: mime_type
plainFields.description: MIME type of the file for content-type validation and compatibility checking.

plainFields.name: file_path
plainFields.description: Storage path or reference to the actual file in the storage system.

plainFields.name: format_approved
plainFields.description: Indicates if the file format has been validated against allowed types (PDF, DOC, DOCX, TXT, ZIP).

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the file attachment was originally created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the file attachment was last modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the file attachment was soft deleted, null if active.

models.name: discussion_board_article_images
models.description:
Image attachments for discussion board articles supporting JPG, PNG, and GIF formats with metadata storage.

Stores metadata for images attached to articles in the discussion board platform. Each image record represents a single image file uploaded by an article author. The actual image files are stored externally while this table maintains metadata including file information, dimensions, and attachment details.

Images are managed exclusively through their parent article context - they cannot exist independently and are always created, accessed, and deleted in relation to the containing article. This ensures proper content ownership and security.

Supports common image formats (JPG, PNG, GIF) with size and dimension tracking for proper display optimization. Soft deletion is supported to maintain audit trails while allowing content moderation.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_article_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged article's {@link discussion_board_articles.id}.

plainFields.name: file_name
plainFields.description: Original filename of the uploaded image as provided by the user.

plainFields.name: file_format
plainFields.description: Image file format. Valid values: JPG, PNG, GIF.

plainFields.name: file_size
plainFields.description: Image file size in bytes for storage and bandwidth management.

plainFields.name: width
plainFields.description: Image width in pixels for display optimization.

plainFields.name: height
plainFields.description: Image height in pixels for display optimization.

plainFields.name: storage_path
plainFields.description: Path or URL to the actual image file in external storage.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the image attachment was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the image attachment was last modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the image attachment was soft deleted, null if active.

models.name: discussion_board_article_tags
models.description:
Junction table for the many-to-many relationship between articles and tags.

Enables articles to have multiple categorization tags and tags to be applied to multiple articles. This supports the tagging system requirement where articles can have up to 10 free-text tags for content organization and filtering.

Each record represents a single tag association to an article, with the composite unique constraint ensuring no duplicate tag assignments. The table uses the standard junction table pattern with foreign keys to both parent entities and a composite primary key for efficient many-to-many relationship management.

Tag associations are managed through article operations, with automatic cleanup when articles or tags are deleted through cascading foreign key constraints.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_article_id
foreignFields.description: Associated article's {@link discussion_board_articles.id}.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_tag_id
foreignFields.description: Associated tag's {@link discussion_board_tags.id}.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the tag was associated with the article.

models.name: discussion_board_tags
models.description:
Tag definitions for article categorization with unique tag names and usage tracking.

Stores standardized tag definitions that can be reused across multiple articles for consistent categorization. Each tag has a unique name that ensures tag normalization and prevents duplicate tags with different spellings or variations.

Tags accumulate usage counts as they are applied to articles, enabling popularity tracking and trending tag identification. Administrators can manage tag definitions to maintain content organization quality across the discussion board.

The unique tag name constraint ensures that articles can be consistently tagged and searched by the same taxonomy. Usage tracking helps identify frequently used tags and those needing cleanup or consolidation.

Soft deletion support allows tags to be archived rather than permanently removed, preserving historical tagging relationships while maintaining system integrity.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Unique tag name used for categorization. Must be unique across the entire system to ensure consistent tagging taxonomy.

plainFields.name: usage_count
plainFields.description: Number of articles that currently use this tag. Incremented when tag is applied to articles and decremented when removed.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the tag definition was first created in the system.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the tag definition was last modified. Updated when tag name changes or usage count updates.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the tag was soft deleted. Null indicates the tag is currently active and available for use.

models.name: discussion_board_comments
models.description:
Main comment table storing comment content, authorship, and timestamps for articles.

Stores individual user comments on articles with immutable publishing timestamps and optional editing capability tracked through snapshot references. Each comment belongs to exactly one article and is authored by exactly one user, maintaining clear ownership relationships.

Comments support basic text content validation similar to articles but with higher relevance weighting for community moderation workflows. The table integrates with snapshot and report tracking for comprehensive comment lifecycle management.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_user_id
foreignFields.description: Comment author's user account reference. {@link discussion_board_users.id}

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_article_id
foreignFields.description: Parent article reference for this comment. {@link discussion_board_articles.id}

plainFields.name: content
plainFields.description: Comment text content with basic formatting support for user discussions.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Immutable timestamp when the comment was originally submitted by the user.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the comment was last modified, used for edit tracking.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp for user/admin comment removal with audit preservation.

models.name: discussion_board_comment_snapshots
models.description:
Historical snapshots of comment edits preserving previous versions for audit trails and moderation transparency.

Captures complete comment state at each edit point, maintaining full edit history with timestamps and content preservation. Used for moderation review, version comparison, and compliance tracking when comment authors modify their content.

Each snapshot links to the original comment through discussion_board_comments.id and contains the exact content state at creation time. The system maintains sequential edit history to track comment evolution.

Snapshots are append-only records that cannot be modified after creation, ensuring audit integrity. When comments are deleted, their snapshots remain preserved for historical reference and moderation audit trails.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_comment_id
foreignFields.description: Original comment's {@link discussion_board_comments.id} that this snapshot preserves.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Original comment title at snapshot creation time.

plainFields.name: body
plainFields.description: Original comment body content at snapshot creation time.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this comment snapshot was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this snapshot record was last updated (system maintenance only).

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp for compliance retention requirements.

models.name: discussion_board_comment_reports
models.description:
User reports of inappropriate comments for moderator review.

Stores reports submitted by users flagging comments as inappropriate, offensive, or violating community guidelines. Each report links to the specific comment being reported and the user submitting the report, with detailed reasons and status tracking for the moderation workflow.

Reports can have statuses including 'pending' (awaiting review), 'reviewed' (under investigation), and 'resolved' (action taken). Moderators use this table to manage comment reports and maintain community standards.

The table maintains timestamps for report submission and resolution, supporting audit trails and moderation performance metrics. Reports remain associated with comments even if the original comment is deleted for historical reference.

Business rules require reports to include substantive reasons (not just generic complaints) and maintain clear links to both the reported comment and reporting user for accountability purposes.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_comment_id
foreignFields.description: Reported comment's {@link discussion_board_comments.id}.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_user_id
foreignFields.description: Reporting user's {@link discussion_board_users.id}.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Detailed reason explaining why the comment was reported as inappropriate, offensive, or violating guidelines. Should be sufficiently descriptive for moderator review.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current status of the report in the moderation workflow. Valid values: pending (awaiting review), reviewed (under investigation), resolved (action completed).

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the report was initially submitted by the user.

plainFields.name: resolved_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the report was resolved by a moderator or administrator.

plainFields.name: moderator_notes
plainFields.description: Additional notes and observations from the moderator reviewing the report, including action taken or justification for dismissal.

models.name: discussion_board_administrator_promotion_requests
models.description:
Stores user requests to become administrators, including request reasons, approval status, and review tracking.

User-submitted applications for administrator privileges that undergo review and approval by super administrators. Each request includes a detailed justification from the applicant and follows a formal workflow from pending approval to final decision.

The table tracks the complete lifecycle of promotion requests including submission, review, approval/rejection, and any feedback provided by reviewing super administrators. Requests remain in the system for audit purposes even after decision.

Foreign key relationships link requests to the submitting user and optionally to the reviewing super administrator when applicable.

foreignFields.name: user_id
foreignFields.description: User who submitted this administrator promotion request. {@link discussion_board_users.id}

foreignFields.name: approved_by_super_administrator_id
foreignFields.description: Super administrator who reviewed and approved this request. {@link discussion_board_super_administrators.id}

foreignFields.name: rejected_by_super_administrator_id
foreignFields.description: Super administrator who reviewed and rejected this request. {@link discussion_board_super_administrators.id}

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: User's written justification for requesting administrator privileges. Must provide detailed reasoning for promotion consideration.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current workflow status of the promotion request. Valid values: pending, approved, rejected.

plainFields.name: decision_reason
plainFields.description: Feedback or explanation provided by the reviewing super administrator for approval/rejection decisions.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the promotion request was initially submitted by the user.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the promotion request record was last modified, including status changes and reviews.

plainFields.name: decision_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the promotion request received a final decision from a super administrator.

models.name: discussion_board_bans
models.description:
Records user bans with comprehensive tracking including ban reasons, durations, and administrator oversight.

Stores all ban actions performed by administrators against users who violate platform policies. Each ban record includes detailed information about the banned user, the administrator who applied the ban, the specific reason for the ban decision, and the ban duration.

Banned users are immediately prevented from logging in through session invalidation workflows. Active sessions of banned users are terminated to ensure immediate enforcement. While banned users cannot access the platform, their existing articles and comments remain visible with appropriate status indicators.

The system supports both temporary and permanent bans with comprehensive audit trails. Administrators can review ban history, modify ban durations, and manually lift bans when appropriate. Ban records are permanently maintained even after bans expire or are lifted to provide complete historical documentation.

Foreign keys establish relationships with the banned user (reference to {@link discussion_board_users.id}) and the administering administrator (reference to {@link discussion_board_administrators.id}), ensuring referential integrity across the ban management system.

foreignFields.name: banned_user_id
foreignFields.description: Banned user's identity reference to {@link discussion_board_users.id}.

foreignFields.name: banning_administrator_id
foreignFields.description: Administrator who applied the ban referencing {@link discussion_board_administrators.id}.

plainFields.name: ban_reason
plainFields.description: Detailed explanation for the ban decision explaining policy violations and justification. Minimum 10 characters required as specified in requirements.

plainFields.name: ban_status
plainFields.description: Current status of the ban. Valid values: active, expired, lifted. Active bans prevent user access, expired bans auto-complete, lifted bans are manually ended.

plainFields.name: ban_start
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the ban becomes effective immediately preventing user authentication and access.

plainFields.name: ban_end
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the ban expires automatically. Null indicates permanent ban requiring manual lifting.

plainFields.name: ban_lifted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when an administrator manually lifted the ban before its scheduled expiration.

plainFields.name: lift_reason
plainFields.description: Optional explanation for why a ban was manually lifted before its scheduled expiration.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Ban record creation timestamp for audit trail and chronological tracking.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last modification timestamp tracking ban status changes and updates.

models.name: discussion_board_administrative_actions
models.description:
Comprehensive audit log tracking all administrative actions performed by administrators across the discussion board platform.

Maintains a complete historical record of administrative activities including section management, content moderation, user banning, promotion approvals, and system configuration changes. Each record captures the administrator who performed the action, the specific action type, target entities involved, timestamps, and detailed action metadata.

The audit trail supports accountability, compliance monitoring, and system transparency by providing administrators with complete visibility into administrative operations. Records are append-only and cannot be modified once created to ensure audit integrity.

Built on snapshot architecture principles to preserve historical accuracy and support forensic analysis of administrative workflows. Action status tracking enables monitoring of workflow completion and identification of failed operations requiring intervention.

Foreign key relationships maintain referential integrity with administrator tables {@link discussion_board_administrators.id}, {@link discussion_board_super_administrators.id} and other target entities across the system.

foreignFields.name: administrator_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the administrator who performed this action, whether regular administrator or super administrator. Links to either {@link discussion_board_administrators.id} or {@link discussion_board_super_administrators.id} based on actor_type.

foreignFields.name: super_administrator_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the super administrator who performed this action, providing specific supervision context. {@link discussion_board_super_administrators.id}

plainFields.name: actor_type
plainFields.description: Type of administrator who performed the action, indicating whether action was performed by a regular administrator ('administrator') or super administrator ('super_administrator'). Determines which foreign key relationship is active.

plainFields.name: action_type
plainFields.description: Type of administrative action performed. Valid values include: section_creation, section_editing, section_deletion, article_deletion, comment_deletion, user_banning, user_unbanning, admin_promotion, admin_demotion, system_config_change.

plainFields.name: target_entity_type
plainFields.description: Type of entity targeted by this action, indicating which table the target_entity_id references. Examples: section, article, comment, user, administrator, system_setting.

plainFields.name: target_entity_id
plainFields.description: Identifier of the specific entity targeted by this administrative action. References the primary key of the table specified by target_entity_type field.

plainFields.name: action_description
plainFields.description: Detailed description of the administrative action performed, including context, rationale, and specific details relevant to the audit trail.

plainFields.name: action_status
plainFields.description: Status of the administrative action indicating whether it was completed successfully or failed. Valid values: pending, completed, failed, cancelled.

plainFields.name: permission_level_required
plainFields.description: Minimum permission level required to perform this action, used for compliance verification and access control auditing. Values: administrator, super_administrator.

plainFields.name: ip_address
plainFields.description: IP address from which the administrative action was performed, providing additional security context for audit purposes.

plainFields.name: user_agent
plainFields.description: Browser or client user agent information from which the action was performed, useful for client context in audit analysis.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the administrative action was initiated and recorded in the audit log.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the administrative action record was last updated, typically when action status changes from pending to completed or failed.

models.name: discussion_board_administrator_hierarchies
models.description:
Tracks administrator grade assignments and promotion/demotion history with complete audit trail.

Manages the two-tier administrator hierarchy system with regular administrators and super administrators. Records all grade changes including who promoted/demoted whom, when the change occurred, and the reason for the action. Maintains historical records for audit purposes and supports the business rule that super administrators cannot demote themselves.

Each record represents a specific grade assignment at a point in time, with new records created whenever an administrator's grade changes. The table ensures proper oversight by documenting which super administrator authorized each promotion or demotion action.

Relationships include references to the user being graded, the super administrator performing the action, and the session context for audit purposes. Temporal fields track when assignments were created, modified, and potentially deleted for soft deletion support.

foreignFields.name: user_id
foreignFields.description: The user being assigned an administrator grade. {@link discussion_board_users.id}

foreignFields.name: super_administrator_id
foreignFields.description: The super administrator who authorized this grade assignment or change. {@link discussion_board_super_administrators.id}

foreignFields.name: super_administrator_session_id
foreignFields.description: The session context in which the promotion/demotion action was performed for audit trail. {@link discussion_board_super_administrator_sessions.id}

plainFields.name: grade
plainFields.description: The administrator grade being assigned: 'administrator' for regular administrators or 'super_administrator' for super administrators.

plainFields.name: action
plainFields.description: The type of action performed: 'promotion' when upgrading grade, 'demotion' when lowering grade, or 'initial_assignment' for first-time assignments.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: The reason or justification for the grade assignment or change, typically copied from promotion request review feedback.

plainFields.name: effective_from
plainFields.description: The date and time when this grade assignment becomes effective and the user gains the corresponding permissions.

plainFields.name: effective_to
plainFields.description: The date and time when this grade assignment expires or is superseded by another assignment. Null indicates currently active assignment.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this grade assignment record was created in the system.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this grade assignment record was last modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this grade assignment was soft-deleted, supporting audit trail preservation while allowing record removal.

models.name: discussion_board_ban_appeals
models.description:
Formal appeals submitted by users contesting ban decisions.

Stores detailed appeal arguments, supporting evidence, and the entire resolution process timeline. Each appeal references a specific ban record and includes comprehensive audit trail of the appeal submission, administrative review, and final resolution.

The appeal process supports user rights to contest moderation actions while maintaining proper administrative oversight. Appeals can have various statuses including pending review, under investigation, approved, or rejected with documented reasoning.

All appeal activities are timestamped and linked to the responsible administrators for complete accountability and transparency in the ban appeal workflow.

foreignFields.name: ban_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the specific ban being appealed. {@link discussion_board_bans.id}

foreignFields.name: user_id
foreignFields.description: User who is appealing the ban decision. {@link discussion_board_users.id}

foreignFields.name: reviewing_administrator_id
foreignFields.description: Administrator assigned to review the appeal. {@link discussion_board_administrators.id}

plainFields.name: appeal_reason
plainFields.description: Detailed reasoning provided by the user explaining why the ban should be overturned. This includes arguments against the ban justification and any supporting evidence or context.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current status of the appeal process. Valid values: pending, under_review, approved, rejected. Determines which administrative workflows apply and controls user access during the appeal period.

plainFields.name: administrator_response
plainFields.description: Official response from the reviewing administrator explaining the appeal decision. This field remains null until the appeal review is completed and provides documented reasoning for the outcome.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the user submitted the formal appeal. This starts the appeal review timeline and triggers notification to administrators.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the last update to the appeal record, including status changes, administrative responses, or user modifications to the appeal argument.

plainFields.name: resolved_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the appeal was officially resolved with a final decision. This field remains null while the appeal is pending or under review.

models.name: discussion_board_moderation_queues
models.description:
Tracks content items (articles and comments) requiring administrative review and moderation.

Maintains a queue of flagged content that requires administrative attention for content quality, policy compliance, or user reports. Each moderation queue entry records the content item reference, reporting user (if applicable), moderator assignment, and resolution status.

Moderation decisions include approval, rejection with removal, or escalation to higher-level administrators. The queue ensures systematic handling of content moderation workflows with proper audit trails and accountability.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_article_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the article requiring moderation. Null when moderating a comment. {@link discussion_board_articles.id}

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_comment_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the comment requiring moderation. Null when moderating an article. {@link discussion_board_comments.id}

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_user_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the user who reported or flagged the content for moderation. Null for system-generated moderation requests. {@link discussion_board_users.id}

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_administrator_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the administrator assigned to handle this moderation request. Null when unassigned. {@link discussion_board_administrators.id}

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Description of why this content requires moderation, including policy violations or quality concerns reported by users or system detection.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current moderation workflow status. Valid values: pending, in_review, approved, rejected, escalated.

plainFields.name: moderation_notes
plainFields.description: Notes from the assigned administrator regarding the moderation decision and rationale.

plainFields.name: escalated_to
plainFields.description: When status is escalated, indicates to whom it was escalated (super_administrator, senior_moderator).

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the moderation request was created and entered into the queue.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the moderation request was last updated, reflecting status changes or assignment updates.

models.name: discussion_board_administrator_permissions
models.description:
Defines specific permissions granted to different administrator grades for role-based access control.

This table establishes the permission matrix that determines what actions each administrator grade can perform within the system. It maps administrator grades (regular administrator, super administrator) to specific permission flags that control access to administrative functions.

The permission system supports granular control over administrative capabilities including section management, content moderation, user banning, and system configuration. Each permission record represents a specific capability that can be granted or revoked for an administrator grade.

Permissions are designed to be extensible, allowing new administrative functions to be added without modifying the core table structure. The system maintains auditability through the relationship with administrative actions and hierarchy management tables.

foreignFields.name: administrator_grade_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the administrator grade this permission applies to. {@link discussion_board_administrator_hierarchies.id}

plainFields.name: permission_code
plainFields.description: Unique code identifier for the specific permission (e.g., 'manage_sections', 'moderate_content', 'ban_users').

plainFields.name: permission_name
